grammar.title: 现在完成时 (Present Perfect Tense)
grammar.structure: 主语 + have/has + 过去分词
grammar.definition: 表示过去发生的动作或状态持续到现在，或对现在有影响。常与already, yet, just, ever, never, for, since等时间状语连用。 用于描述从过去开始持续到现在的情况，或强调过去的经验对现在的影响。

examples.en: We have got quite used to them.
examples.zh: 我们已经相当习惯它们了。

examples.en: Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
examples.zh: 一些所谓的'现代'作品已经展出将近八十年了。

examples.en: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture.
examples.zh: 即使对艺术不感兴趣的人也一定会注意到现代雕塑。

grammar.title: 被动语态 (Passive Voice)
grammar.structure: 主语 + be + 过去分词 (+ by + 动作执行者)
grammar.definition: 当句子的主语是动作的承受者时使用被动语态。强调动作的接受者或当动作执行者不重要时使用。 用于强调动作的承受者，或当动作执行者未知、不重要时。

examples.en: The spheres had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other.
examples.zh: 这些球已被磁化，彼此相互吸引或排斥。

examples.en: Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.

examples.en: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes.
examples.zh: 火花从小黑盒子里发射出来。

grammar.title: 情态动词 + have + 过去分词 (Modal + Perfect Infinitive)
grammar.structure: 情态动词 + have + 过去分词
grammar.definition: 表示对过去发生的事情的推测、评论或可能性。must have done表示肯定推测，can't have done表示否定推测。 用于表达对过去事件的推测或判断。

patterns.pattern: Some + 名词 + have been + 过去分词 + for + 时间段

original.en: Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
original.zh: 一些所谓的'现代'作品已经展出将近八十年了。

patterns.pattern: These + 名词 + were designed to + 动词原形

original.en: These peculiar forms not only seemed designed to shock people emotionally, but to give them electric shocks as well!

patterns.pattern: Even + 主语 + cannot have failed to + 动词原形

original.en: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
original.zh: 即使对艺术不感兴趣的人，也不可能没注意到公共场所展出的现代雕塑。

imitations.en: Even students who hate history cannot have failed to notice this famous painting.

lines.en: Modern sculpture rarely surprises us any more.
lines.zh: 现代雕塑不再使我们感到惊讶了。

lines.en: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
lines.zh: 那种认为现代艺术只能在博物馆里才能看到的观点是错误的。

lines.en: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
lines.zh: 即使是对艺术不感兴趣的人也不会注意到在公共场所展示的现代艺术品。

lines.en: Strange forms stand in gardens, and outside buildings and shops. We have got quite used to them. Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
lines.zh: 公园里、大楼和商店外竖立着的奇形怪状的雕塑，对这些，我们已经司空见惯了。

lines.en: In spite of this, some people -- including myself -- were surprise by a recent exhibition of modern sculpture.
lines.zh: 有些所谓的“现代”艺术品在那里已经陈列了近80年了。

lines.en: The first thing I saw when I entered the art gallery was a notice which said: 'Do not touch the exhibits.
lines.zh: 尽管如此，最近举办的一次现代雕塑展览还是使一些人（包括我在内）大吃了一惊。

lines.en: Some of them are dangerous! The objects on display were pieces of moving sculpture.
lines.zh: 走进展厅首先看到的是一张告示，上面写着“切勿触摸展品，某些展品有危险！

lines.en: Oddly shaped forms that are suspended form the ceiling and move in response to a gust of wind are quite familiar to everybody.

lines.zh: 人们所熟悉的是悬挂在天花板上、造型奇特、随风飘荡的雕塑品。

lines.en: Lined up against the wall, there were long thin wires attached to metal spheres.
lines.zh: 这些展品却使人大开眼界。

lines.en: The spheres had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
lines.zh: 靠墙排列着许多细长的电线，而电线又连着金属球。

lines.en: In the centre of the hall, there were a number of tall structures which contained coloured lights.
lines.zh: 金属球经过磁化，互相之间不停地相互吸引或相互排斥。

lines.en: These lights flickered continuously like traffic lights which have gone mad.
lines.zh: 展厅中央是装有彩色灯泡的许多高高的构件，灯泡一刻不停地闪烁着，就像失去了控制的红绿灯。

lines.en: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes and red lamps flashed on and off angrily.
lines.zh: 小黑盒子里迸出火花，红色灯泡发怒似地忽明忽暗。

lines.en: It was rather like an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment.
lines.zh: 这儿倒像是在展览古老的电子设备。

lines.en: These peculiar forms not only seemed designed to shock people emotionally, but to give them electric shocks as well!
lines.zh: 好像设计这些奇形怪状的展品不仅是为了给人感情上的强烈刺激，而且还想给人以电击似的！

questions.q: How might some of the exhibits have been dangerous?
questions.zh: 这些展品怎么会具有危险性呢？
questions.a: They were pieces of moving sculpture: magnetized metal spheres that attracted and repelled each other, continuously flickering lights, small black boxes emitting sparks, and they could even give people electric shocks.
questions.aZh: 它们是活动雕塑：被磁化、不停相吸相斥的金属球，不停闪烁的灯光，迸出火花的小黑盒，甚至还会给人电击。
questions.hint: 答案在课文后半段：展品是 pieces of moving sculpture，金属球被磁化，末尾说它们 give them electric shocks as well。

questions.q: What mistaken idea about modern art does the writer mention?
questions.zh: 作者提到关于现代艺术的哪种错误观点？
questions.a: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
questions.aZh: 那种认为现代艺术只能在博物馆里才能看到的观点是错误的。
questions.hint: 课文第二句 The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.

questions.q: What was the first thing the writer saw when he entered the art gallery?
questions.zh: 作者走进美术馆时首先看到的是什么？
questions.a: A notice which said: 'Do not touch the exhibits. Some of them are dangerous!'
questions.aZh: 一张告示，上面写着“切勿触摸展品。某些展品有危险！”
questions.hint: 课文: The first thing I saw when I entered the art gallery was a notice which said...

questions.q: What were the objects standing against the wall?
questions.zh: 靠墙排列着的展品是什么样的？
questions.a: There were long thin wires attached to metal spheres which had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
questions.aZh: 那里有细长的电线，连着被磁化的金属球，金属球一直相互吸引或相互排斥。
questions.hint: 课文: Lined up against the wall, there were long thin wires attached to metal spheres.

questions.q: Why does the writer compare the exhibition to 'an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment'?
questions.zh: 作者为什么把这个展览比作“古老的电子设备展览”？
questions.a: Because the tall structures with continuously flickering coloured lights, the sparks emitted from small black boxes and the angrily flashing red lamps looked crude and old-fashioned, yet seemed alive with electricity.
questions.aZh: 因为装有不停闪烁的彩色灯泡的高大构件、小黑盒迸出的火花和发怒似忽明忽暗的红灯，看起来粗糙而陈旧，却充满了电流的动感。
questions.hint: 结合课文倒数第二句 It was rather like an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment 与其前后对灯光、火花的描写作答。

translation:
现代雕塑不再使我们感到惊讶了。
那种认为现代艺术只能在博物馆里才能看到的观点是错误的。
即使是对艺术不感兴趣的人也不会注意到在公共场所展示的现代艺术品。
公园里、大楼和商店外竖立着的奇形怪状的雕塑，对这些，我们已经司空见惯了。
有些所谓的“现代”艺术品在那里已经陈列了近80年了。
尽管如此，最近举办的一次现代雕塑展览还是使一些人（包括我在内）大吃了一惊。
走进展厅首先看到的是一张告示，上面写着“切勿触摸展品，某些展品有危险！
”展品都是些活动的雕像。
人们所熟悉的是悬挂在天花板上、造型奇特、随风飘荡的雕塑品。
这些展品却使人大开眼界。
靠墙排列着许多细长的电线，而电线又连着金属球。
金属球经过磁化，互相之间不停地相互吸引或相互排斥。
展厅中央是装有彩色灯泡的许多高高的构件，灯泡一刻不停地闪烁着，就像失去了控制的红绿灯。
小黑盒子里迸出火花，红色灯泡发怒似地忽明忽暗。
这儿倒像是在展览古老的电子设备。
好像设计这些奇形怪状的展品不仅是为了给人感情上的强烈刺激，而且还想给人以电击似的！
title: Electric Currents in Modern Art
subtitle: 现代艺术中的电流

lead.question: 看似普通的现代雕塑展，为什么会让观众觉得危险，甚至可能遭到电击？
lead.warmup: 一提到现代艺术，很多人会想到美术馆里静静摆放的绘画和雕塑。但本文作者却在一次现代雕塑展上大开了眼界：展品不再是静止的，而是会动、会闪、还会放电的装置。参观者刚进门就看到“切勿触摸，某些展品有危险”的告示。想弄懂作者为什么把这场展览比作“史前电子设备展”，就跟着课文一起走进这座奇特的展厅吧。
goals: 掌握 current / electric / sculpture / gallery / magnet / flicker / emit 等本课核心词汇。
理解 be attached to、in response to、be familiar to、take no interest in 等固定搭配。
复习被动语态，以及 that 引导的同位语从句和 which 引导的定语从句。
能用英语描述一件展品，并说明它为什么会使人感到危险。
lead.summary: 本文从现代雕塑已司空见惯谈起，指出人们误以为现代艺术只能在博物馆里看到，其实它早已出现在公共场所。接着作者描述一次令他吃惊的展览：靠墙的金属球经磁化后不停相吸相斥，展厅中央的高大构件里彩灯疯狂闪烁，小黑盒迸出火花，红灯怒闪。这些展品像古老电子设备，仿佛专为刺激人的情感、甚至给人电击而设计。
lead.tips: emit 是重读闭音节动词，过去式和过去分词要双写 t 写作 emitted，且多用被动 be emitted from，指火花、光、声音等从某处“散发出来”。

exercises.q: 汉译英：现代雕塑不再使我们感到惊讶了。
exercises.a: Modern sculpture rarely surprises us any more.
exercises.note: rarely 表否定，“不再”用 any more

exercises.q: 填空：The first thing I saw when I entered the art ______ was a notice.
句型转换（改被动）：Workers emitted sparks from small black boxes.
exercises.a: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes.
exercises.note: emit 过去分词双写 t，作被动

exercises.q: 改错：The idea which modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
exercises.a: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
exercises.note: 同位语从句用 that，不用 which

exercises.q: 填空：The spheres had been ______ (magnet) and attracted or repelled each other.
exercises.note: magnetize 变过去分词，此处为被动

exercises.q: 汉译英：这些灯不停地闪烁着，就像失去控制的红绿灯。
exercises.a: These lights flickered continuously like traffic lights which have gone mad.

exercises.q: 填空：An electric ______ flows through the wires and lights the bulbs.
exercises.note: current 指电流，也可指水流

quiz.q: 作者认为下列哪种观点是错误的？
options: The idea that modern sculpture is always dangerous.
The idea that public places should hold no art.
The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums.
The idea that all exhibits must be modern.
quiz.note: 课文第二句点明该观点错误

quiz.q: 作者走进展厅时首先看到了什么？
options: A piece of moving sculpture hanging from the ceiling.
A notice warning visitors not to touch the exhibits.
A long thin wire attached to a metal sphere.
A number of tall structures with coloured lights.
quiz.note: 先看到的是“切勿触摸”的告示

quiz.q: 靠墙排列着的展品是什么？
options: Small black boxes emitting sparks.
Tall structures containing coloured lights.
Oddly shaped forms suspended from the ceiling.
Long thin wires attached to metal spheres.

quiz.q: 关于那些金属球，下列哪项说法正确？
options: They were fixed to the ceiling and moved in the wind.
They flickered continuously like traffic lights.
They had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
They were made of coloured glass and emitted sparks.
quiz.note: 金属球被磁化，不停相吸相斥

quiz.q: 展厅中央那些高大构件里有什么？
options: Coloured lights which flickered continuously.
Magnetized metal spheres.
Small black boxes full of sparks.
Notices warning of danger.
quiz.note: 构件里是彩色灯泡，不停闪烁

quiz.q: 作者把这个展览比作什么？
options: An exhibition of modern oil paintings.
A museum of ancient sculpture.
A mad traffic light system.
An exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment.
